title: Tokens
teaser: How AI actually reads your words

basics.say: Here's a secret: AI doesn't read words the way you do. It reads tokens.
A token is a small chunk of text – a whole word, part of a word, or even a single character.
Look: 'Prompting' becomes two tokens, 'Prompt' and 'ing'. Short, common words are usually one token each.
This sentence is 9 tokens for 35 characters. In English, a token is roughly three quarters of a word.
Why care? Tokens decide how much the AI can read at once, how fast it answers and what it costs.

deeper.say: Each AI model has its own tokenizer, so the same sentence can be a different number of tokens from one model to another.
Other languages often need more tokens than English for the same idea. So do code, numbers and rare words.
Paid AI services usually charge per token – both the tokens you send and the tokens the model writes back.
Want to see it live? Press 'Try it yourself' and type any sentence – you'll see exactly how it gets chopped up.

takeaway: AI reads chunks, not words – and every chunk counts.
